summary: Solaris 10 and earlier use a non-POSIX shell that doesn't expand Ansible's default ~/.ansible/tmp, causing module failures; set remote_tmp to $HOME/.ansible/tmp or set ansible_shell_executable to a POSIX shell like /usr/xpg4/bin/sh.
questions: Modules fail on my Solaris 10 hosts, why?
How do I make Ansible use a POSIX shell on Solaris?
Can I set remote_tmp per host?

answer_card.title: Fix module failures on Solaris
answer_card.answer_md:
Solaris ≤ 10's default shell doesn't expand `~/.ansible/tmp`. Either:

- Set `remote_tmp` to a path the shell expands correctly:

```ini
[defaults]
remote_tmp = $HOME/.ansible/tmp
```

or per host: `host1 ansible_remote_tmp=$HOME/.ansible/tmp`.
- Use a POSIX shell: `solaris1 ansible_shell_executable=/usr/xpg4/bin/sh` (bash, ksh, zsh also work).
